This page exists to prove tier T2 works end to end. Both engines below boot in
your browser; nothing is computed on a server.

Every cell is editable. Change a number, press **Run**, and see what happens —
that is the entire reason this tier exists.

## Python (Pyodide)

The same data generating process as `pylib/dgp.py`, written out in full so you
can edit it. It plants a known effect and then checks whether a naive
difference in means recovers it.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
#| min-lines: 18
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def confounded(n=2000, ate=2.0, confounding=3.0, seed=7):
    """x drives both the probability of treatment and the outcome."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    x = rng.normal(0, 1, n)
    p = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-confounding * x))
    t = rng.binomial(1, p)
    y0 = 10 + confounding * x + rng.normal(0, 1, n)
    y1 = y0 + ate
    y = np.where(t == 1, y1, y0)
    return pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "t": t, "y0": y0, "y1": y1, "y": y})

df = confounded(confounding=3.0)

true_ate = (df["y1"] - df["y0"]).mean()
naive = df.loc[df["t"] == 1, "y"].mean() - df.loc[df["t"] == 0, "y"].mean()

print(f"True ATE:         {true_ate:.3f}")
print(f"Naive difference: {naive:.3f}")
print(f"Bias:             {naive - true_ate:+.3f}")
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Set `confounding=0.0` and run it again. The bias collapses to sampling noise,
because at zero the design is a randomized experiment.
:::

## Python — check the decomposition yourself

Chapter 1 claims that the naive difference equals ATT plus selection bias.
That is an identity, so it should hold exactly, not approximately.

```{pyodide}
#| min-lines: 12
treated = df[df["t"] == 1]
control = df[df["t"] == 0]

att = (treated["y1"] - treated["y0"]).mean()
selection_bias = treated["y0"].mean() - control["y0"].mean()
naive = treated["y"].mean() - control["y"].mean()

print(f"ATT:            {att:.6f}")
print(f"Selection bias: {selection_bias:.6f}")
print(f"Sum:            {att + selection_bias:.6f}")
print(f"Naive:          {naive:.6f}")
print(f"Difference:     {abs(att + selection_bias - naive):.2e}")
```

The residual should be at floating-point noise level. If it is not, the
identity has been misstated — which is exactly the kind of error this tier is
here to catch.

## R (WebR)

The same check in R, to confirm the second engine is alive.

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
#| min-lines: 16
set.seed(7)
n <- 2000
confounding <- 3.0
ate <- 2.0

x  <- rnorm(n)
p  <- 1 / (1 + exp(-confounding * x))
t  <- rbinom(n, 1, p)
y0 <- 10 + confounding * x + rnorm(n)
y1 <- y0 + ate
y  <- ifelse(t == 1, y1, y0)

true_ate <- mean(y1 - y0)
naive    <- mean(y[t == 1]) - mean(y[t == 0])

cat(sprintf("True ATE:         %.3f\n", true_ate))
cat(sprintf("Naive difference: %.3f\n", naive))
cat(sprintf("Bias:             %+.3f\n", naive - true_ate))
```

::: {.recall}
Browser-side execution is not a lesser version of running code locally — it
removes the setup step entirely. But its package set is limited to pure-Python
and wasm-built wheels, so anything with compiled extensions still belongs in
the build-time tier.
:::
